summary: Iteration 21 — BoothIQ v2.21 validation. Backend: 6/6 pytest pass (100%). (1) POST /api/crm/leads/bulk-assign now returns {ok:true, updated:N, prev:[{lead_id, account_manager_id}]} — verified prev captures the previous owner for each lead in the batch, before the reassign is applied. (2) POST /api/crm/leads/restore-assign {assignments:[{lead_id, account_manager_id}]} correctly restores each lead's previous owner and sets routing_reason='Reassignment undone', returning {ok:true, restored:N}. Full reassign→restore round-trip round-trips the assignment cleanly (also verified for the case where prev owner was auto-routed post-create). (3) POST /api/crm/notifications/digest/run?window_hours=24 (lead_manager) returns {reps_notified:int, total_leads:int} (returned 200 in ~2s in preview; total_leads=410+). AM role is correctly forbidden (403). (4) Import execute (distribute=person, assignee_id=<lead_manager>) completes with counts and creates the lead assigned to the chosen person — the per-import immediate email has been removed and execute no longer raises. (5) GET /api/crm/leads?claim_mismatch=true still returns only flagged leads (every row has claim_mismatch=true). Web (leadmanager@boothiq.com/639201, REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL): (a) Leads page — selected 2 lead-select-<id> rows, chose 'Account Manager' in bulk-assign-am, clicked bulk-assign-btn, reassign-confirm-text reads 'Reassign 2 leads to Account Manager? They'll be notified by email and push.', clicking reassign-confirm-btn triggers bulk-assign; sonner toast shows 'Reassigned 2 lead(s) to Account Manager' with an 'Undo' action button (10s duration); clicking Undo hits /crm/leads/restore-assign and shows toast 'Undone — restored 2 lead(s)' — VERIFIED in-screenshot. (b) Lead Detail — Section header now reads 'Change History' (renamed from 'Edit History' in v2.20); hist-tab-all / hist-tab-updated / hist-tab-assigned / hist-tab-status testIDs all present; selecting a tab narrows the list correctly (on a sample lead: all=2, updated=0, assigned=2, status=0; narrowing invariant all>=each subset holds). (c) Mismatch Report — nav-mismatch-report opens /crm/mismatch-report; empty state 'No claim mismatches' renders correctly when no flagged leads exist (backend tests rolled back their imports). Row rendering was validated in iteration_20 with the same schema (mismatch-row-<id>). No console errors, no red screens. Push still 500s in preview due to placeholder EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY — expected and swallowed by notify_assignment_summary.
critical_code_review_comments: routes_crm.py:346-368 bulk_assign — prev captures BEFORE update_many, using find with {'id': {'$in': ids}}. If some ids are invalid, they are silently omitted from prev (count of prev may be < len(lead_ids)); this is fine because restore only acts on entries it receives. Consider returning updated_ids too for auditability.

routes_crm.py:375-394 restore_assign — Iterates assignments and does one update per lead. For very large undo batches, a bulk operation grouped by previous owner would be more efficient, but current UX (a Ctrl-Z-style toast on a single bulk-assign) is bounded and fine.
routes_digest.py:22 — Query uses ISO string range on 'routed_at'. Since routed_at is stored via now_iso() (also ISO 8601 UTC), lexical comparison is correct. Good.

routes_digest.py:46-52 — send_email is best-effort per rep. If Resend key becomes invalid, the digest silently reports reps_notified<total, which is correct but may hide a systemic email outage. Consider exposing last_error in the response for manager visibility.

routes_digest.py:62-80 digest_worker — Uses app_settings with _id=DIGEST_KEY. On first-ever run it only records a baseline and never sends — good anti-blast behavior. However, on backend restart it re-reads the last_run so it still respects the 24h window. Good.
routes_import.py:378 — Per-import email path removed; execute is fully sync-safe. Confirmed no notify call remains in execute().

success_rate.frontend: 100% (undo toast+restore, hist tabs all present + narrowing, mismatch report route + empty state)
